front: Charlemagne fut couronné empereur en l'an 800.
pronunciation: [shar-luh-MAN-yuh fü koo-roh-nay ahn-puh-RUHR ahn lahn wee-SAHN]
back: Charlemagne was crowned emperor in the year 800.
context: In Rome, by Pope Leo III. French schoolchildren are told he 'invented' school.

front: Jeanne d'Arc fut brûlée vive à Rouen en 1431.
pronunciation: [zhahn DARK fü brü-lay VEEV ah roo-AHN ahn meel kah-truh-sahn-trahnt-AN]
back: Joan of Arc was burned alive in Rouen in 1431.
context: She led the French during the Hundred Years' War and was canonized in 1920.

front: Le massacre de la Saint-Barthélemy eut lieu en 1572.
pronunciation: [luh mah-SAH-kruh duh lah san bar-tay-luh-MEE ü LYUH ahn meel san-sahn swah-sahnt-DOOZ]
back: The St. Bartholomew's Day massacre took place in 1572.
context: Thousands of Protestants were killed during the Wars of Religion.

front: Henri IV a signé l'édit de Nantes en 1598.
pronunciation: [ahn-REE KAHTR ah see-nyay lay-dee duh NAHNT ahn meel sank-sahn-kah-truh-van-dee-WEET]
back: Henry IV signed the Edict of Nantes in 1598.
context: It granted Protestants religious freedom. Louis XIV revoked it in 1685.

front: Louis XIV était surnommé le Roi-Soleil.
pronunciation: [lwee kah-TORZ ay-teh sür-noh-may luh rwah-soh-LAY]
back: Louis XIV was nicknamed the Sun King.
context: He reigned 72 years (1643–1715) and built Versailles.

front: L'État, c'est moi.
pronunciation: [lay-TAH, seh MWAH]
back: I am the State.
context: Attributed to Louis XIV as the motto of absolute monarchy, though he probably never said it.

front: Sous l'Ancien Régime, la société était divisée en trois ordres.
pronunciation: [soo lahn-syan ray-ZHEEM, lah soh-syay-TAY ay-teh dee-vee-zay ahn trwah ZOR-druh]
back: Under the Ancien Régime, society was divided into three estates.
context: The clergy, the nobility and the Third Estate.

front: La prise de la Bastille a eu lieu le 14 juillet 1789.
pronunciation: [lah preez duh lah bas-TEE ah ü LYUH luh kah-torz zhwee-YEH meel set-sahn kah-truh-van-NUHF]
back: The storming of the Bastille took place on July 14, 1789.
context: Now the Fête nationale. The French never call it 'Bastille Day'; they say 'le 14 Juillet'.

front: Les hommes naissent et demeurent libres et égaux en droits.
pronunciation: [lay ZUM nes ay duh-muhr LEE-bruh ay ay-GOH ahn DRWAH]
back: Men are born and remain free and equal in rights.
context: Article 1 of the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (August 1789).

front: Louis XVI fut guillotiné en 1793.
pronunciation: [lwee SEZ fü gee-yoh-tee-NAY ahn meel set-sahn kah-truh-van-TREZ]
back: Louis XVI was guillotined in 1793.
context: Marie-Antoinette followed nine months later.

front: Sous la Terreur, Robespierre fit exécuter des milliers de suspects.
pronunciation: [soo lah teh-RUHR, roh-bes-PYEHR fee teg-zay-kü-tay day mee-lyay duh süs-PEH]
back: During the Terror, Robespierre had thousands of suspects executed.
context: 1793–94. He was guillotined himself in July 1794.

front: Qu'ils mangent de la brioche !
pronunciation: [keel mahnzh duh lah bree-OSH]
back: Let them eat cake!
context: Wrongly attributed to Marie-Antoinette; Rousseau wrote it before she arrived in France.

front: Napoléon se fit sacrer empereur à Notre-Dame en 1804.
pronunciation: [nah-poh-lay-OHN suh fee sah-kray ahn-puh-RUHR ah noh-truh-DAM ahn meel wee-sahn-KAHTR]
back: Napoleon had himself crowned emperor at Notre-Dame in 1804.
context: He took the crown from the Pope and placed it on his own head.

front: Le Code civil reste l'héritage le plus durable de Napoléon.
pronunciation: [luh kod see-VEEL rest lay-ree-TAHZH luh plü dü-RAH-bluh duh nah-poh-lay-OHN]
back: The Civil Code remains Napoleon's most lasting legacy.
context: Promulgated in 1804, it still underpins French law and inspired codes worldwide.

front: Il a connu son Waterloo.
pronunciation: [ee lah koh-nü sohn wah-tehr-LOH]
back: He met his Waterloo.
context: Napoleon's final defeat in 1815, now any crushing failure.

front: Les Trois Glorieuses ont renversé Charles X en 1830.
pronunciation: [lay trwah gloh-RYUHZ ohn rahn-vehr-say sharl DEES ahn meel wee-sahn-TRAHNT]
back: The Three Glorious Days overthrew Charles X in 1830.
context: Painted by Delacroix in 'La Liberté guidant le peuple'.

front: L'esclavage a été définitivement aboli en 1848.
pronunciation: [les-klah-VAHZH ah ay-tay day-fee-nee-teev-mahn tah-boh-LEE ahn meel wee-sahn-kah-rahnt-WEET]
back: Slavery was definitively abolished in 1848.
context: Thanks to Victor Schœlcher. A first abolition in 1794 was reversed by Napoleon in 1802.

front: Le baron Haussmann a transformé Paris sous le Second Empire.
pronunciation: [luh bah-rohn ohs-MAN ah trahns-for-may pah-REE soo luh suh-gohn tahn-PEER]
back: Baron Haussmann transformed Paris under the Second Empire.
context: The grand boulevards and cream-stone buildings date from 1853–1870.

front: La Commune de Paris fut écrasée en mai 1871.
pronunciation: [lah koh-mün duh pah-REE fü tay-krah-ZAY ahn meh meel wee-sahn swah-sahnt-ON-zuh]
back: The Paris Commune was crushed in May 1871.
context: The 'Semaine sanglante' (Bloody Week) left thousands dead.

front: Jules Ferry a rendu l'école gratuite, laïque et obligatoire.
pronunciation: [zhül feh-REE ah rahn-dü lay-kol grah-TWEET, lah-EEK ay oh-blee-gah-TWAHR]
back: Jules Ferry made school free, secular and compulsory.
context: The Ferry laws of 1881–82, a pillar of the Republic.

front: L'affaire Dreyfus a profondément divisé la France.
pronunciation: [lah-fehr dreh-FÜS ah proh-fohn-day-mahn dee-vee-zay lah FRAHNS]
back: The Dreyfus affair deeply divided France.
context: A Jewish army officer was falsely convicted of treason in 1894 and cleared in 1906.

front: La loi de 1905 a séparé les Églises et l'État.
pronunciation: [lah lwah duh meel nuhf-sahn-SANK ah say-pah-ray lay zay-GLEEZ ay lay-TAH]
back: The 1905 law separated the Churches and the State.
context: The legal foundation of 'la laïcité'.

front: Les poilus ont tenu à Verdun en 1916.
pronunciation: [lay pwah-LÜ ohn tuh-nü ah vehr-DAN ahn meel nuhf-sahn-SEZ]
back: The French soldiers held out at Verdun in 1916.
context: 'Un poilu' (hairy one) = a WWI French soldier. The battle lasted ten months.

front: Il n'y a pas un village sans son monument aux morts.
pronunciation: [eel nyah pah zan vee-LAHZH sahn sohn moh-nü-mahn oh MOR]
back: There isn't a village without its war memorial.
context: Nearly 1.4 million French soldiers died in WWI.

front: Le Front populaire a instauré les congés payés en 1936.
pronunciation: [luh frohn poh-pü-LEHR ah an-stoh-ray lay kohn-zhay peh-YAY ahn meel nuhf-sahn trahnt-SEES]
back: The Popular Front introduced paid holidays in 1936.
context: Two weeks at first; French workers flocked to the seaside for the first time.

front: Le 18 juin 1940, de Gaulle lance son appel depuis Londres.
pronunciation: [luh dee-zweet ZHWAN meel nuhf-sahn kah-RAHNT, duh GOHL lahns sohn nah-PEL duh-pwee LOHN-druh]
back: On June 18, 1940, de Gaulle makes his appeal from London.
context: The BBC broadcast that founded Free France. The historical present is common in French history writing.

front: La France a perdu une bataille ! Mais la France n'a pas perdu la guerre !
pronunciation: [lah FRAHNS ah pehr-dü ün bah-TAHY ! meh lah FRAHNS nah pah pehr-dü lah GEHR]
back: France has lost a battle! But France has not lost the war!
context: From de Gaulle's 1940 poster 'À tous les Français'.

front: Le régime de Vichy a collaboré avec l'occupant.
pronunciation: [luh ray-zheem duh vee-SHEE ah koh-lah-boh-ray ah-vek loh-kü-PAHN]
back: The Vichy regime collaborated with the occupier.
context: Led by Marshal Pétain, 1940–44.

front: Jean Moulin a unifié les mouvements de la Résistance.
pronunciation: [zhahn moo-LAN ah ü-nee-fyay lay moov-mahn duh lah ray-zees-TAHNS]
back: Jean Moulin unified the Resistance movements.
context: Arrested and tortured by the Gestapo in 1943. His ashes are in the Panthéon.

front: Paris outragé ! Paris brisé ! Paris martyrisé ! Mais Paris libéré !
pronunciation: [pah-REE oo-trah-ZHAY ! pah-REE bree-ZAY ! pah-REE mar-tee-ree-ZAY ! meh pah-REE lee-bay-RAY]
back: Paris outraged! Paris broken! Paris martyred! But Paris liberated!
context: De Gaulle's speech at the Hôtel de Ville, August 25, 1944.

front: Les Françaises ont voté pour la première fois en 1945.
pronunciation: [lay frahn-SEZ ohn voh-tay poor lah pruh-myehr FWAH ahn meel nuhf-sahn kah-rahnt-SANK]
back: French women voted for the first time in 1945.
context: The right was granted in 1944; late compared with much of Europe.

front: Les Trente Glorieuses ont transformé le pays.
pronunciation: [lay trahnt gloh-RYUHZ ohn trahns-for-may luh peh-YEE]
back: The Thirty Glorious Years transformed the country.
context: The postwar boom, 1945–1975: growth, cars, TV and suburbs.

front: La guerre d'Algérie a duré de 1954 à 1962.
pronunciation: [lah gehr dal-zhay-REE ah dü-RAY duh meel nuhf-sahn sank-sahnt-KAHTR ah meel nuhf-sahn swah-sahnt-DUH]
back: The Algerian War lasted from 1954 to 1962.
context: For decades officially called 'les événements' (the events).

front: Je vous ai compris !
pronunciation: [zhuh voo zay kohm-PREE]
back: I have understood you!
context: De Gaulle in Algiers, 1958: a famously ambiguous phrase, heard differently by each side.

front: La Ve République est née en 1958.
pronunciation: [lah sank-YEM ray-pü-BLEEK eh nay ahn meel nuhf-sahn sank-sahnt-WEET]
back: The Fifth Republic was born in 1958.
context: Its constitution gave strong powers to the president.

front: Sous les pavés, la plage !
pronunciation: [soo lay pah-VAY, lah PLAHZH]
back: Beneath the paving stones, the beach!
context: A May 68 slogan: students dug up cobblestones and found sand beneath.

front: Il est interdit d'interdire.
pronunciation: [ee leh tan-tehr-DEE dan-tehr-DEER]
back: It is forbidden to forbid.
context: Another May 68 slogan, now quoted ironically.

front: Mai 68 a bouleversé les mœurs de la société française.
pronunciation: [meh swah-sahnt-WEET ah bool-vehr-say lay MUHRS duh lah soh-syay-tay frahn-SEZ]
back: May 68 transformed the social mores of French society.
context: Student protests and a general strike of ten million workers.

front: Robert Badinter a fait abolir la peine de mort en 1981.
pronunciation: [roh-behr bah-dan-TEHR ah feh tah-boh-leer lah pen duh MOR ahn meel nuhf-sahn kah-truh-van-ON]
back: Robert Badinter had the death penalty abolished in 1981.
context: Under President Mitterrand. Badinter entered the Panthéon in 2025.

front: La cohabitation oblige le président à gouverner avec l'opposition.
pronunciation: [lah koh-ah-bee-tah-SYOHN oh-bleezh luh pray-zee-DAHN ah goo-vehr-nay ah-vek loh-poh-zee-SYOHN]
back: Cohabitation forces the president to govern with the opposition.
context: When the president and parliamentary majority are from rival camps (1986, 1993, 1997).

front: Le gouvernement a eu recours au 49.3.
pronunciation: [luh goo-vehr-nuh-mahn ah ü ruh-koor oh kah-rahnt-nuhf TRWAH]
back: The government resorted to Article 49.3.
context: It lets the government pass a law without a vote, at the risk of a no-confidence motion.

front: Le passage à l'euro a eu lieu en 2002.
pronunciation: [luh pah-sahzh ah luh-ROH ah ü lyuh ahn duh-meel-DUH]
back: The switch to the euro happened in 2002.
context: Many French people still convert big prices into francs.

front: Le mouvement des gilets jaunes est né en 2018.
pronunciation: [luh moov-mahn day zhee-leh ZHOHN eh nay ahn duh-meel-dee-WEET]
back: The yellow vests movement began in 2018.
context: Triggered by a fuel tax, it grew into a broad protest movement.

front: Les Français ont la Révolution dans le sang.
pronunciation: [lay frahn-SEH ohn lah ray-voh-lü-SYOHN dahn luh SAHN]
back: The French have revolution in their blood.
context: A cliché, but strikes and demonstrations remain part of political life.

front: L'histoire est un perpétuel recommencement.
pronunciation: [lees-TWAHR eh tan pehr-pay-twel ruh-koh-mahns-MAHN]
back: History repeats itself.
context: A saying derived from Thucydides.
